title: 原创示例 · 阅读理解

passage: Many people think learning a language is only about memorizing words. In fact, the most important part is using it in real life.
A student who talks with friends every day will improve faster than one who only reads books. Practice, not perfection, is the key.
items.q: What does the passage mainly say?
o: Books are more useful than talking
Using the language matters more than just memorizing
Memorizing words is the only key
items.ex: 主旨题。文章强调"在真实生活中使用语言"比"只背单词"更重要，B 最符合。

passage: A small daily habit can lead to big changes. Spending just ten minutes a day on English adds up to over sixty hours a year.
items.q: How many hours a year does ten minutes a day add up to?
items.ex: 数字题。10 分钟 × 365 天 ≈ 3650 分钟 ≈ 60.8 小时，超过 60 小时，选 C。

title: 原创示例 · 词汇单选

items.q: He tried to ________ his mistake, but it was too late.
items.ex: correct = 纠正；collect=收集；cancel=取消；count=数。句意"他试图纠正错误，但太晚了"，选 A。

title: 词汇基础（一）· 高频动词与搭配

items.q: Please ________ me if you have any questions about the course.
items.ex: tell sb sth（告诉某人某事）后面直接跟人；say 后面接说的内容；speak 后面常接语言；talk 常与 to / with 连用。句意「有问题请告诉我」，选 tell。

items.q: The meeting has been ________ until next Monday because of the storm.
items.ex: put off = 推迟；put on = 穿上、上演；put up = 举起、搭建；put out = 扑灭。句意「会议因暴风雨推迟到下周一」，选 put off。

items.q: She ________ three hours doing her homework last night.
items.ex: spend 的主语是人，结构是 spend time (in) doing；take 常用 it takes sb some time to do；cost 的主语是物；pay 常与 for 连用。主语是 she，选 spent。

items.q: If you do not hurry, you may ________ the last bus.
items.ex: miss 指「错过（车、机会）」；lose 指「丢失」；drop 指「掉落」；leave 指「离开、留下」。句意「错过末班车」，选 miss。

items.q: The new rule will ________ into effect next month.
items.ex: come into effect（生效）是固定搭配；go / get / take 都不能与 into effect 组成这个意思。句意「新规定下个月生效」，选 come。

items.q: The teacher ________ us to read the text aloud.
items.ex: ask sb to do sth（请某人做某事）；promise sb to do 是「答应某人自己去做」，主语不对；hope 和 suggest 都不能接 sb to do。句意「老师让我们朗读课文」，选 asked。

items.q: It is not easy to ________ up smoking.
items.ex: give up（放弃、戒除）是固定搭配，give up smoking 即「戒烟」；put up 举起；take up 开始从事、占用；set up 建立。选 give。

items.q: Please ________ your dictionary with you tomorrow.
items.ex: bring 指「带到说话人这边来」；take 指「带离说话人」；fetch 指「去取了再回来」；carry 指「搬运」，不含方向。句意是「明天带来」，选 bring。

items.q: We should ________ the waste paper instead of throwing it away.
items.ex: recycle = 回收利用；replace = 取代；refuse = 拒绝；remove = 移走。与 throwing it away（扔掉）对应的正是「回收」，选 recycle。

items.q: The two sides finally ________ an agreement after a long talk.
items.ex: reach an agreement（达成协议）是固定搭配；arrive 后要接 at；come 后要接 to；get 不直接接 an agreement。选 reached。

items.q: She is used to ________ up early in the morning.
items.ex: be used to 里的 to 是介词，后面接动名词 doing，表示「习惯于」；used to do 才是「过去常常」。选 getting。

items.q: Could you ________ me a favour and open the window?
items.ex: do sb a favour（帮某人一个忙）是固定搭配；make / take / give 都不能与 favour 组成这个意思。选 do。

items.q: Please ________ out this form and return it to the office.
items.ex: fill out（填写）与 fill in 同义，fill out the form 即「填表」；put out 扑灭；take out 取出；work out 算出。选 fill。

items.q: We must ________ the plan carefully before we start.
items.ex: discuss 是及物动词，直接跟宾语；talk 和 speak 后面需要接 about 或 to；say 后面接说的内容。所以去掉介词后只能用 discuss，选它。

items.q: The school ________ the students with free books.
items.ex: provide sb with sth（给某人提供某物）是固定搭配；offer 要用 offer sb sth；give 要用 give sb sth，都不能与 with 连用。选 provided。

items.q: I have no ________ what he is talking about.
items.ex: have no idea（不知道）是固定表达；thought / opinion / mind 都不能用在这个结构里。选 idea。

items.q: It is important to ________ a good habit of reading.
items.ex: form（或 develop）a habit 指「养成习惯」；fix 是「固定、修理」；set 常与 up 连用；make 不与 habit 搭配。选 form。

items.q: They ________ the problem in a simple way.
items.ex: solve the problem（解决问题）是固定搭配；answer 后面接 question；reply 和 respond 后面常接 to。选 solved。

items.q: Do not ________ your time on things that do not matter.
items.ex: waste time on sth 指「把时间浪费在……上」；save 是「节省」，与 do not matter 的语境相反；keep 和 leave 都不构成该搭配。选 waste。

items.q: We should ________ the instructions carefully before using the machine.
items.ex: follow the instructions 指「按说明操作」；look / see / watch 都是「看」，不能与 instructions 构成这个意思。选 follow。

title: 词汇基础（二）· 名词、形容词与搭配

items.q: She has a good ________ of English grammar.
items.ex: a good command of English（熟练掌握英语）是固定搭配；order 指「命令、顺序」；control 指「控制」；power 指「力量、权力」。选 command。

items.q: The doctor gave me some useful ________ about keeping healthy.
items.ex: advice 是不可数名词，没有复数形式，some 后直接用；suggestion 和 tip 是可数名词，some 后要用复数。选 advice。

items.q: There is little ________ of rain this month.
items.ex: chance 是名词，There is little chance of…（……的可能性很小）；possible 和 likely 是形容词，able 也是形容词，都不能在 there be 结构里作主语。选 chance。

items.q: He is ________ of his own mistakes now.
items.ex: be aware of（意识到）与 mistakes 搭配通顺；be proud of 是「为……骄傲」，不会为错误骄傲；be afraid of 是「害怕」；kind 后一般接人。选 aware。

items.q: The book is ________ reading, especially for beginners.
items.ex: be worth doing（值得做）中 worth 后面直接接动名词；worthy 要写成 be worthy of being read；worthwhile 要写成 It is worthwhile to read；valuable 不与 reading 搭配。选 worth。

items.q: He works hard and is ________ of praise.
items.ex: be worthy of praise（值得表扬）是固定搭配；proud 后面接的是自己骄傲的对象；full of 是「充满」；short of 是「缺少」。选 worthy。

items.q: There is a big ________ between the two answers.
items.ex: a big 后面需要名词 difference；different 是形容词；differ 是动词；differently 是副词，都不能被 a big 修饰。选 difference。

items.q: The teacher praised him for his good ________ in class.
items.ex: 介词 for 后面接名词 performance（表现）；perform 是动词原形；performing 和 performed 都是动词形式。选 performance。

items.q: After a long walk, they felt very ________.
items.ex: tired 修饰人的感受，指「感到累」；tiring 修饰令人疲倦的事物；tire 是动词；tiredness 是名词，不能被 very 修饰。这里主语是 they，选 tired。

items.q: This is the most ________ film I have ever seen.
items.ex: interesting 修饰事物，指「有趣的」；interested 修饰人的感受，要说 be interested in；interest 是名词或动词；interestingly 是副词。修饰 film 用 interesting。

items.q: His answer was ________, so nobody agreed with him.
items.ex: was 后面需要形容词作表语，只有 wrong 符合；error、fault、mistake 都是名词。选 wrong。

items.q: The company needs someone with rich working ________.
items.ex: experience 表示「经验」时是不可数名词；experiences 指一次次的「经历」；experienced 是形容词；experiencing 是动词形式。选 experience。

items.q: We should pay attention to the ________ of the environment.
items.ex: 定冠词 the 后面需要名词 protection；protect 是动词；protected 和 protective 都是形容词形式。选 protection。

items.q: He has made great ________ in his English study.
items.ex: progress 是不可数名词，不能加 s，make progress（取得进步）是固定搭配；progressive 是形容词；progressing 是动词形式。选 progress。

items.q: The traffic in this city is very ________ in the morning.
items.ex: heavy traffic（交通拥堵）是固定搭配；weighty 指「沉重的、有分量的」（多形容话语、责任）；big 和 large 都不与 traffic 搭配。选 heavy。

items.q: It is our ________ to take care of our parents when they are old.
items.ex: duty 指「义务、责任」；right 是「权利」；habit 是「习惯」；chance 是「机会」。句意「照顾年老的父母是我们的义务」，选 duty。

items.q: Be ________! The baby is sleeping.
items.ex: quiet 指「安静、不吵闹」；calm 指「镇定」；still 指「静止不动」；slow 指「慢」。句意是别吵醒婴儿，选 quiet。

items.q: The old man lives ________, but he never feels lonely.
items.ex: alone 作副词表示「独自地」，修饰 live；lonely 是形容词，表示「孤独的（心情）」；lone 只作定语形容词；loneliness 是名词。选 alone。

items.q: You need to make a ________ before the deadline.
items.ex: make a decision（做决定）是固定搭配，a 后面需要名词；decide 是动词；decisive 是形容词；decided 是动词过去式或形容词。选 decision。

items.q: The medicine had a good ________ on his illness.
items.ex: have an effect on（对……有影响、有效果）是固定搭配，effect 是名词；affect 是动词；result 用 result of；cause 用 cause of。选 effect。

title: 语法基础（一）· 时态、语态与从句

items.q: He ________ to school by bike every day.
items.ex: every day 提示一般现在时；主语 he 是第三人称单数，动词要加 s，选 goes。go 用于 I / you / we / they；going 需要与 be 连用；gone 是过去分词，前面要有 have。

items.q: Look! The children ________ football on the playground.
items.ex: Look! 是现在进行时的典型标志词，表示此刻正在发生，选 are playing。一般现在时 play 表示习惯；played 是过去；have played 强调对现在的影响，都不符合「此刻正在」。

items.q: I ________ my homework when my mother came back.
items.ex: when 引导的从句用一般过去时 came，表示「那一刻」，主句要用过去进行时表示「当时正在做」，选 was doing。did 表示做完了，与 when 的插入感冲突；do 与 am doing 时态不匹配。

items.q: By the end of last year, he ________ in that factory for ten years.
items.ex: by the end of last year 是「过去的时间点」，动作在那之前已经持续十年，属于「过去的过去」，用过去完成时 had worked。has worked 是现在完成时，需要与 now / so far 这类现在时间连用。

items.q: The homework ________ by the students yesterday.
items.ex: 主语 homework 是动作的承受者，且时间是 yesterday，用一般过去时的被动语态 was finished。finished 是主动；is finished 时态不对；finishes 是一般现在时主动。

items.q: If it ________ tomorrow, we will stay at home.
items.ex: if 引导的条件状语从句中，主句用将来时，从句要用一般现在时表将来，选 rains。will rain 是中式英语最常见的错法；rained 与 is raining 与 tomorrow 都矛盾。

items.q: This is the boy ________ helped me yesterday.
items.ex: 先行词 the boy 指人，且在从句里作主语，用关系代词 who。which 指物；whose 表示所属；where 指地点，都不能在从句里作主语。

items.q: He speaks English ________ than his brother.
items.ex: than 提示用比较级，well 的比较级是 better，选它。well 是原级，good 是形容词原级，不能修饰动词 speaks；best 是最高级，用在三者以上比较，不能与 than 连用。

items.q: It is important ________ we should keep our promise.
items.ex: It 是形式主语，真正的主语是后面那个意思完整的从句，用 that 引导且 that 不作成分、不翻译。what 要在从句里充当成分；which 表示「哪一个」；whether 表示「是否」，都与句意不符。

items.q: Neither Tom nor his parents ________ at home last night.
items.ex: neither…nor… 连接两个主语时，谓语要与**最近的那个主语**一致。离谓语最近的是 his parents（复数），且时间是 last night，所以用 were。

items.q: He suggested that we ________ the meeting until next week.
items.ex: suggest 作「建议」讲时，后面的从句用 (should) + 动词原形，should 可以省略，所以填 put off。puts off 与 will put off 都不符合该结构；putting off 是动名词，不能作从句谓语。

items.q: Not only he but also I ________ interested in music.
items.ex: not only…but also… 连接两个主语时，谓语与最近的主语一致。离谓语最近的是 I，所以用 am。is 对应第三人称单数，are 与 were 都不与 I 搭配。

title: 选词填空（一）· 日常语境单空

passage: Learning a language takes time and patience.
items.q: If you practise a little every day, you will make ________ progress.
items.ex: steady progress 指「稳定的进步」，与「每天练一点」呼应；sudden 是「突然的」；rare 是「稀有的」；silent 是「沉默的」，都不能修饰 progress 的这个意思。

passage: Tom got up late this morning.
items.q: As a ________, he missed the first bus.
items.ex: as a result（结果、因此）是固定短语，承接前面「起晚了」；sum 只在 in sum（总而言之）里用；whole 只在 as a whole（总体上）里用；matter 不与 as a 搭配。

passage: The final exam is only two weeks away.
items.q: You had better ________ your notes every day.
items.ex: review 意为「复习」，与 notes 搭配自然；refuse 是「拒绝」；remove 是「移走」；reply 是「回答」。只有 review 与「考前」的语境相符。

passage: Mary has wanted to help sick people since she was a child.
items.q: She is going to ________ medicine at university.
items.ex: study medicine 指「学医」，是固定搭配；stay、stand、stop 都不能与 medicine 组成这个意思。

passage: Our city is building a new public library.
items.q: It will be ________ to the public next spring.
items.ex: be open to the public（向公众开放）中 open 是形容词作表语，表示状态；opening 是动名词或现在分词；opens 是动词第三人称单数；openly 是副词，都不能作 be 后面的表语。

passage: He failed the driving test twice.
items.q: But he did not ________ up and tried a third time.
items.ex: give up（放弃）是固定搭配，与 but 的转折语气一致；put up 举起；take up 开始从事；set up 建立。

passage: The students are preparing for an English speech contest.
items.q: Each of them has to ________ a topic first.
items.ex: choose a topic 指「选定一个话题」；chase 是「追赶」；change 是「改变」；charge 是「收费、充电」。语境是准备比赛，选 choose。

passage: My grandmother is over eighty years old.
items.q: She still keeps a ________ diet and exercises every morning.
items.ex: a balanced diet（均衡饮食）是固定搭配；broken 指「破损的」；bitter 指「苦的」；basic 指「基本的」，都不与 diet 构成固定说法。

passage: The train was late again this morning.
items.q: Many passengers ________ about the poor service.
items.ex: complain about（抱怨……）是固定搭配；compare 是「比较」；complete 是「完成」；compete 是「竞争」。句意是乘客抱怨服务差，选 complained。

passage: Reading English aloud is a good habit for beginners.
items.q: It can help you ________ your pronunciation.
items.ex: improve pronunciation 指「改进发音」；increase 用于数量增加；invent 是「发明」；invite 是「邀请」。只有 improve 能与 pronunciation 搭配。

passage: The little boy got lost in the shopping mall.
items.q: Luckily, a security guard ________ him find his mother.
items.ex: help sb (to) do sth 是固定结构，help 后可以接动词原形；hope 不能接 sb do；hate 后面接 doing 或 to do，不接 sb do；hurry 意思是「匆忙」，不接这个结构。

passage: Time is limited for everyone.
items.q: We should make good ________ of every minute.
items.ex: make good use of（充分利用）是固定搭配；make one's way 意思是「前进、前往」；part 和 side 都不能与 make…of 组成这个意思。

title: 阅读理解（一）· 校园与生活

passage: Li Ming studies in a small town. Every morning he rides his bike to school, and the trip takes about twenty minutes.
He says riding keeps him healthy and saves money, though it is hard on rainy days.
items.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Riding a bike brings Li Ming both good points and bad points.
Li Ming hates going to school.
Li Ming's school is very far from his home.
Li Ming wants to buy a car.
items.ex: 第一句说骑车上学，第二句用 though 转折指出「雨天难受」，是典型的两面性，A 概括最全。B 文中无依据；文中说二十分钟，算不上 very far，C 过度；D 完全没提。

passage: A survey shows that students who take notes by hand remember more than those who type on a laptop.
Writing slows you down, so you have to decide what is really important.
items.q: Why do students who write by hand remember more?
o: Because writing forces them to choose the key points.
Because laptops are too heavy to carry.
Because notes taken by hand are easier to read.
items.ex: 第二句给出原因：写字慢，所以必须判断什么才重要，正是 A。B/C/D 文中都没有出现，属于凭常识编出来的干扰项。

passage: The school library opens at eight in the morning and closes at nine in the evening.
Students can borrow up to five books at a time, and each book can be kept for thirty days.
items.q: How long can a student keep a book?
items.ex: 第二句直接说「每本书可借三十天」，数字对应 A。B/C/D 是拿文中的「五本」「八点」「九点」凑出来的干扰项，问的是天数，不能拿这些数字顶上。

passage: Many people throw away food they cannot finish at restaurants.
Some cities now ask restaurants to offer smaller plates, and this simple change has cut waste a lot.
items.q: What does the passage say about smaller plates?
o: They make the food taste better.
They are more expensive than big plates.
They are only used at home.
items.ex: 末句说「这个简单的改变减少了很多浪费」，与 A 完全对应。B/C/D 文中均无提及。

passage: Zhang Wei joined the school running club last term.
At first he could only run one kilometre, but now he can run five without stopping.
items.q: What can we learn about Zhang Wei?
o: He has made progress in running.
He runs faster than everyone else in his class.
items.ex: 「一开始只能跑一公里，现在能跑五公里」说明的是进步，选 A。B 与事实相反；C 文中没提生病；文中只说距离变长，没比较速度，D 过度推断。

passage: Sleep is important for study. Students who sleep less than six hours often find it hard to focus in class.
Going to bed at the same time every night helps the body get used to a healthy rhythm.
items.q: What is suggested at the end of the passage?
o: Sleeping more than ten hours a day.
items.ex: 末句建议「每晚在同一时间上床」，也就是保持规律作息，选 A。B/C/D 都不是文章给出的建议。

passage: The new subway line will open next month. It connects the airport with the city centre, and the trip will take only half an hour.
Tickets will be cheaper than a taxi ride.
items.q: What is one advantage of the new subway line?
o: It is faster than a plane.
items.ex: 「只要半小时」对应省时，「比打车便宜」对应省钱，选 A。文中没和飞机比过速度，B 无依据；只是便宜不是免费，C 错；D 文中没提运行时段。

passage: Doing part-time jobs can help students learn to manage money.
However, working too many hours may leave them too tired to study.
items.q: What is the writer's attitude towards part-time jobs?
o: They are useful if the working hours are controlled.
They are only suitable for poor students.
items.ex: 文章先说好处，再用 However 指出「时间过多就影响学习」，态度是**有条件地支持**，选 A。B 与「有帮助」矛盾；C 与「影响学习」矛盾；D 文中根本没提家庭条件。

title: 阅读理解（二）· 学习与科技

passage: AI tools can now translate a whole page in a second.
But translation is not the same as understanding: a machine may miss the feeling behind a sentence.
items.q: What does the passage warn about?
o: Machines may lose the meaning behind the words.
Translation tools are too slow to be useful.
Nobody needs to learn a foreign language now.
AI is able to read our minds.
items.ex: 第二句点明「机器可能错过句子背后的情感」，正是 A。第一句说「一秒钟」，与「太慢」相反，B 错；C 是文中没有的结论；D 属于夸张，文中无据。

passage: Many students use apps to memorise new words.
Research shows that words reviewed at growing intervals stay in memory longer than words reviewed all at once.
items.q: What does the research suggest?
o: Reviewing words at increasing intervals works better.
Apps are useless for learning words.
Students should stop using paper dictionaries.
items.ex: 「间隔逐渐拉长地复习」正是 A 的意思。文章没有否定 app，B 过度；「一次复习完就够」与原文相反，C 错；D 文中完全没提。

passage: Online courses let people study at any time they like.
However, without a fixed timetable, many learners give up after a few weeks.

The courses usually cost too much.
The teachers are not well trained.
The video lessons are too long.

passage: The number of e-books borrowed from the city library doubled last year.
Readers say they like looking up a word easily, but some still miss the feel of paper.
items.q: What do some readers still miss?
o: The feeling of reading on paper.
items.ex: 末句 the feel of paper 就是指纸质书的手感，与 A 对应。其余选项都没有出现在文中。

passage: A new study finds that a short walk after lunch helps students stay awake in the afternoon class.
The walk should last about ten minutes.
items.q: How long should the walk be?
items.ex: 第二句直接给出「大约十分钟」，选 A。其余数字文中都没有出现。

passage: Some people say technology makes us lazy, because we no longer remember phone numbers.
Others argue that we simply use our memory for more useful things.
items.q: What does the passage show?
o: An effective way to improve memory.
How to use a smartphone safely.
items.ex: 文章用 Some… Others… 并列了两种相反的看法，选 A。B/C/D 都不是文章的内容。

passage: The city has opened a free coding class for primary school students.
The class was so popular that the number of seats was raised twice.
items.q: What does the passage tell us about the class?
o: It was much more popular than expected.
It was too expensive for most families.
It was cancelled after one week.
It was only open to university students.

passage: A: The gym is open from six in the morning to ten at night.
B: The swimming pool is closed for cleaning every Monday.
C: Students can book a tennis court on the school website.
D: A new yoga class will start next month.
items.q: Which of the following is closed on one certain day each week?

passage: A: The canteen serves breakfast until nine thirty.
B: Several vegetarian dishes have been added to the menu.
C: A new card payment system starts on the first of next month.
D: There is usually a short queue at lunch time.
items.q: What will start working on the first of next month?

B: The study room provides free water and Wi-Fi.

items.q: What must you do if you lose a book you have borrowed?

B: A robot competition will be held in May.

passage: A: The bus to the airport leaves every thirty minutes.
B: Tickets can be bought on the phone.
C: The last bus leaves at ten at night.

B: It also shows your weekly progress in a simple chart.

items.q: Which of the following is free for a period of time?

B: Please keep your voice down after ten at night.

o: Keep your voice down after ten

passage: Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities. Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the ficld and influencing the kind of research that gets published. Men were found to account for 60of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the jourmals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers. The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience—a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly. Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and ncuroscicncc. Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. passage: Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year. Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction. These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. In 2015, the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason- excused or unexcused- is a primary cause of low academic achievement. Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. After all, if students don't show up, teachers can't teach them. But what if America's attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face- such as being ejected from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness? As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children's academic achievement. We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning. In fact, children with no unexcused absences- but 15 to 18 excused absences- have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences. Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none. We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of school challenges affect children's academic progress. Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction. How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy. School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences. These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction. They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. We find neither to be the case. As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often. We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.

Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision making priority. And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability. passage: As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are likeminded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organised ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organisations, and families. Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity. What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: “...a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people.” In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labour. One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism (社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy is sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group. Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others. But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the youand-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other—in recognition that one’s fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterised by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.

passage: People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency. Under the guise (外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however. These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations. When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesirable result. If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone’s feelings of self-worth, an outright (直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict. The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. As uncomfortable as it may make you continuously receiving unwanted advice, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely diffuse much faster. Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety. It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual’s underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.
